newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Namibia mulls hydro-electric scheme with Angola.
newsitem.headline: Namibia mulls hydro-electric scheme with Angola.

text.p: Namibia is conducting a feasibility study for a hydro-electric scheme on the Kunene River bordering Angola to make it self-sufficient in power, an official said on Tuesday.

The study is focused on a dam at Epupa Falls and no decision had been taken yet by the Angolan or Namibian governments, said Piet Heyns, a director in Namibia's water ministry. The study should be completed by the end of the year, he said.

"Epupa is a favourable site because it will be able to generate electricity all year round because it can store all the run off in a rainy season unlike other sites we have considered," Heyns told Reuters.

The proposed hydro-electric plant would cost over one billion Namibian dollars ($224 million) and could generate 400 megaWatts of power, more than meeting the 220 megaWatts the country currently used, he said.
He was among over 100 delegates from southern African and European countries attending a conference on water sharing in sub-Saharan Africa held in the tiny landlocked kingdom of Lesotho.
